Title: A scratched phone, a slimmer belly and life by the lake
NewsSummary: Our mascot is overjoyed to see students start to return to our campuses.
NewsContent:
Our mascot is overjoyed to see students start to return to campus after spending such a long time away from the University during the pandemic. The last few months have been very unusual for AKU's leopard who opens up about the experience on campus in this outspoken interview.

Where have you been?

Well in February this year - it seems so very, very long ago - I was in East Africa to celebrate with our graduating students in Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda. I've never been one to miss an opportunity, so I went off to visit my cousins in Masai Mara national park and lunched on warthogs and antelope. There was so much food but I was missing Karachi and so I caught a flight back just before international travel shut down. 

As if that was not excitement enough, the Karachi campus soon became eerily empty with no students around, everyone seemed just to have just vanished. Interestingly, I noted a new fashion trend at the hospital! Blue everywhere, everyone was wearing lots of layers of the colour above their clothes and blue face coverings too. It was a little like Halloween in blue with everyone dressed up as smurfs!

I was confused until one of the nursing students set me at ease. He enlightened me about the novel virus going around, the 'lockdown', on the need to regularly wash my paws and to pull a mask over my whiskers, mouth and nose. 

I noticed things changing quickly around campus as the hard-working people at our hospital set up new spaces to care for patients and a separate testing zone. Just as I was getting used to things again, I heard that they were shutting down the Sports and Rehabilitation Center, where I set up my lair, so I had to find another green, bushy place to call home.

Where did you go?

I looked all around the campus for the perfect spot. At first, I went to CIME but like last year the cat was in no mood to share her territory. I tried to convince her that there's a lot more space since the crocodile left but she just wouldn't listen. 

I love greenery and needed a place where I could scratch the ground, so I chose to stay by the lake. It's nice and warm and everyone is friendly, except the ducks of course! Also, I blend in with the green so I have some privacy too. 

While the move was a little unsettling at first, I knew that I wasn't alone. If I had to get used to being in a new place, students had to get used to studying at home, away from the campus. That thought gave me the courage to persevere and adapt to my new surroundings. 

What has been different about campus?

People have been behaving a little differently on campus. I noticed a lot of people elbowing each other when they met which was odd. I thought humans used to shake hands! People also tend to stand at a distance from one another. I'm used to it now but it seemed really awkward at the beginning.

Overall, there have been fewer people around but I've noticed more squirrels and birds too, especially in the courtyards. 

Since the staff at the hospital seemed to be very busy, I took care to not get in their way. 

How has life been different for you?

Constantly wearing a mask is a little uncomfortable as it tickles against my whiskers and it always comes off when I jump on a tree. 

I was getting a bit bored at the start of the lockdown as I heard you were not supposed to leave your home. So I stayed at the lake and I took up yoga to pass the time. I feel so much more flexible right now. Also, my belly is gone since I'm not eating the leftover food that people used to give me at the Sports Centre. While I do miss the days when students would share their biryani with me, I understand that sharing food and eating in groups is a big, big risk right now. 

After so many months of waiting for students to come back, I was so glad to hear about things starting to return to normal. Yesterday, I saw a student wearing a t shirt with my picture on it and I felt like a celebrity just like I did when I first appeared!

Now that students are trickling back, do you have any message for them? 

It's just fantastic to have you back! I'm so glad to see all of you taking precautions by wearing masks. Just like you all, I also use the Sehat Check app everyday too. Although I may need to get a new phone as my paws keep scratching the screen!

I'm particularly proud of the final year nursing and medical students who wear personal protective equipment during their rounds and continue to tend to patients. It must take a lot of courage and perseverance to serve patients in these difficult times and by keeping yourself safe you are playing a part in keeping everyone at AKU and your families safe. 

But while I'm happy to see those already on campus, I'm also eagerly awaiting the other years to join us back too. I'd like to tell those in the early years of their studies that they'll be back soon as I gather the return is being managed in phases. Don't worry you still have plenty of time to spend with me, and on campus! For those still studying online, please be patient. I'm sure we'll see you as soon as arrangements are made.

Students, particularly those in their master's programme, may be dealing with disruptions to their research projects and some students could be worried about graduation. I'd urge them to take things one day at a time. I know things will keep on getting better as more and more students return. And when things improve further, we'll be able to open up the student lounges and be together like in the good old days.

I also look forward to visiting our other campuses in Pakistan, England, Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda to meet you all. I haven't met my relatives at Nairobi National Park and London Zoo for so long too so it would be nice to catch up with them as well.

In short, I can't wait to see more of you all very soon.
